title: Page oscillation and memory threshold exploratory notes
body:
Summary:
This is a working log for an exploratory investigation into observed page oscillation (repeated migrations/paging of KV cache pages), hysteresis around eviction thresholds, and the interaction with memory bandwidth and pipeline stalls. Goal is to surface a reproducible signal, sanity-check our telemetry, and propose conservative mitigations for Dedicated and Private deployments where customers have long-tail sequences and aggressive batch packing.

Motivation / Why this matters:
- Several customer incidents (see JIRA RT-789) show tail latency spikes that correlate with sustained per-GPU memory bandwidth approaching 80–90% on 80GB machines.
- Hypothesis: when KV residency falls below a soft threshold, our eviction warmup/prefetch heuristics oscillate between evicting and immediately re-fetching hot pages, generating extra DRAM traffic and CPU-GPU DMA churn.
- This increases per-token latency variance and reduces effective throughput despite average token throughput appearing unchanged.

High-level hypothesis threads to test:
1) There is a hysteresis band for eviction decisioning: too narrow -> oscillation; too wide -> cache bloat and memory pressure.
2) Prefetch/warmup policies that are reactive to single-request miss events increase paging when multi-tenant interleaving occurs.
3) Aggregate memory bandwidth (not just occupancy) correlates stronger with tail latency than simple resident set size.

Testbed / Setup:
- Hardware: 4x A100S nodes (80GB) and 2x RTX-8000 nodes (48GB) for cross-hw sanity.
- Runtime: canary build 2025-01-28 (kv-prefetch-refactor branch) and baseline main@2024-11-01.
- Models: mix of L2-large (seq 2048) and L3-chatty (seq 512) to exercise KV differential reuse.
- Workloads: synthetic replay of customer A and B traces (trace-a.high-longtail, trace-b.multiuser).
- Metrics collected: per-page access counts, last-access timestamp histogram, eviction attempt timestamps, DMA bytes/sec per GPU, CPI-like stall counters, scheduler queue depths.
- Tools: perf, nvprof, custom KV telemetry export to /tmp/kv-osc-experiments/ (jsonlines).

Experiment matrix (notes):
- Exp 1: Baseline eviction: LRU-ish with 5% soft headroom. Record tail latency, reuse rate p90/p99, total DMA bytes.
- Exp 2: Increase hysteresis band by widening soft headroom from 5% -> 20%.
- Exp 3: Add a simple cooldown window: once a page is evicted, suppress prefetch of that page for 100–500ms (param sweep).
- Exp 4: Change prefetch trigger from single-miss to miss-rate over sliding 1s window (threshold sweep).
- Exp 5: Simulate tenant interleaving (two tenant traces alternating) to stress cross-tenant churn.

Quick raw observations (sanity-first pass):
- Baseline (Exp1) on trace-a: p95 latency spikes coincide with bursts of DMA activity; reuse rate drops immediately before spikes.
- When hysteresis widened (Exp2) p95 improved by ~12% and p99 improved by ~20% for trace-a, but average resident set increased by ~8% (more RAM used).
- Cooldown window (Exp3) eliminated many small oscillation spikes; best results at cooldown = 200ms. Too long (>=500ms) caused misses to persist for heavy context-switching workloads.
- Prefetch rate-based trigger (Exp4) reduced unnecessary prefetch storms under interleaving; misses moved to slightly earlier in sequences but bandwidth usage smoothed out.

Representative numeric excerpt (trace-a, A100S, warm-run):
- Baseline: p50=12ms, p95=142ms, p99=340ms, DMA=1.9GB/s sustained during spikes, reuse_rate_p95=0.62
- Wider hysteresis: p50=13ms, p95=125ms, p99=270ms, DMA=1.6GB/s, reuse_rate_p95=0.66
- Cooldown(200ms): p50=13ms, p95=118ms, p99=210ms, DMA=1.3GB/s, reuse_rate_p95=0.69

Telemetry deep-dive notes:
- Page access autocorrelation: found repeating 120–260ms periodicity on pages that later got evicted and re-referenced — suggests a user-visible cadence (e.g., streaming responses).
- DMA bursts align to eviction followed by prefetch within 10–50ms. Prefetch path amplifies DRAM reads because several nearby pages are warmed up in one RPC.
- NVLink utilization shows brief spikes (20–40ms) synchronous across GPUs when multi-tenant interleave occurs, implying coordinator-level prefetch decisions cause cross-GPU traffic.
- Stall counters (CPU-side) show increased wait-for-device jitter during oscillation windows; likely backpressure cascades to scheduler.

Interpretation / working theory:
- The eviction decision currently only considers instant occupancy and last-access recency. In steady multi-tenant or long-tail workloads this leads to thrashing around a nearly-critical working set size.
- Prefetch being tied to single-request heuristics makes the system amplify small misses into bursts of device DMA as it attempts to pre-warm spatially-adjacent pages.
- Memory bandwidth is a stronger predictor of tail latency than absolute RSS because repeated read/warmup cycles saturate DRAM channels and create contention on DMA engines.

Checks on instrumentation fidelity (notes to self):
- KV telemetry timestamps in trace exporter had a ~15ms clock skew vs. perf sampling earlier; need to align clocks across processes.
- Ensure dma bytes/sec in exporter are delta-sampled per 100ms (we currently had 1s resolution in baseline runs, causing smoothing).

Candidate mitigations (ranked conservative -> aggressive):
1) Hysteresis band: increase soft-headroom default from 5% -> 15% in release candidate; quick win for Dedicated.
2) Eviction cooldown: suppress immediate prefetch for recently-evicted pages for 150–250ms; tune via canary.
3) Prefetch aggregation: coalesce prefetch operations so that multiple prefetch requests are scheduled in a batched DMA window rather than immediate per-miss. Reduces NVLink spikes.
4) Miss-rate-based prefetch: switch from single-miss trigger to rate-window trigger to avoid reacting to transient misses.
5) Adaptive bandwidth-aware throttling: if DMA/sec > X (configurable), throttle background prefetch/fill jobs until below threshold.

Risk notes and tradeoffs:
- Wider hysteresis increases resident set size -> potential OOM scenarios on very memory-constrained customers (private on 48GB). Must gate with per-customer mem limits and fallbacks.
- Cooldown might hurt worst-case cold-start latency for some single-session heavy sequences. Need to measure warming impact for L3-chatty.
- Aggressive aggregation could delay some legitimate prefetches, increasing first-byte latency for very sparse sequences.

Action items (short):
- [Priya] open PR with hysteresis default bump and feature flag (PR draft linked).
- [Liam] run cross-hw sanity suite for cooldown=100/200/300ms and produce p50/p95/p99 delta table (due 2025-02-20).
- [Marco] add higher-res DMA sampling to exporter (100ms) and fix clock sync across agent processes (due 2025-02-18).
- [Aisha] create a canary plan for Dedicated customers with >=2TB GPU RAM pool (template in Confluence CONFLUENCE-RT-KV-012).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do these mitigations interact with quantized models that have different tokenization reuse patterns? Need a small study.
- Can we build a lightweight estimator in the scheduler that predicts oscillation propensity for a route in real-time? Feels like an ML signal and maybe part of Optimize.
- Validate for on-prem: does NUMA/dom placement change the hysteresis sweet spot? Early signs from RTX-8000 runs show narrower band needed.

Rough notes / stream-of-consciousness (keep for context):
- saw one run that looked identical to the baseline until tenant switch at t=2m30s, then oscillation started — suggests some cross-tenant working set interference boundary.
- consider exposing a per-customer "eviction-aggressiveness" knob in Console for Dedicated customers with ops-safety guardrails.

References & links:
- JIRA RT-789 (incident)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/432
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-RT-KV-012 (canary run template)

Appendix: quick experiment log snippets (copied from /tmp/kv-osc-experiments):
- 2025-01-21T14:32:11Z | exp=baseline | dma=1.92GB/s | p99=342ms | eviction_count=1842 | reuse_p95=0.61
- 2025-01-21T14:45:06Z | exp=hysteresis20 | dma=1.56GB/s | p99=266ms | eviction_count=1320 | reuse_p95=0.68
- 2025-01-22T09:12:07Z | exp=cooldown200 | dma=1.31GB/s | p99=208ms | eviction_count=1183 | reuse_p95=0.70

If anything looks surprising / you want a narrower export of the raw telemetry I can push a filtered jsonlines with per-page timelines. Also happy to pair with Marco on the perf markers to reduce instrumentation noise.

-- Priya
(Notes kept intentionally informal; will convert to a PR description + Confluence summary if consensus on mitigation path emerges.)
